title: Automatically classifying emails into activities
abstract: Studies activity-centered email management and the problem of recognizing whether an incoming email belongs to an ongoing user activity. It evaluates reply-thread and Naive Bayes baselines alongside similarity methods using participants and message content, and combines multiple signals for activity assignment.
venue: Proceedings of the 11th International Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces (IUI 2006)

title: Business Process Instances Discovery from Email Logs
abstract: Proposes an unsupervised method for discovering business-process instances from professional email logs. The method first groups emails by semantic process model and then combines multiple email attributes to identify messages belonging to individual process instances, making it directly relevant to message-to-work-instance correlation.
venue: 2017 IEEE International Conference on Services Computing (SCC)

title: Mining Business Process Activities from Email Logs
abstract: Presents an unsupervised approach for mining business-process information from email logs. Emails are grouped by process model and then subdivided and labeled into business-activity types using semantic representations including LSA and Word2vec.

title: Multi-level clustering for extracting process-related information from email logs
abstract: Uses multi-level unsupervised clustering to extract process-related information from professional email logs. The approach associates emails with process/activity structures and learns activity labels that can subsequently be used to recognize newly arriving emails.
venue: 2017 11th International Conference on Research Challenges in Information Science (RCIS)

title: A framework for mining process models from emails logs
abstract: Introduces a framework for mining business-process models from professional email using unsupervised learning with limited human intervention. The framework addresses which business process and activity an email represents and which emails belong to the same process instance, and evaluates the approach on a real-world email dataset containing two process models.

title: On the elicitation and annotation of business activities based on emails
abstract: Studies discovery and annotation of business-process activities from email. Beyond activity labels, it extracts metadata such as participant roles, attachment types, and link domains, providing evidence about observable signals associated with organizational work activities.
venue: Proceedings of the 34th ACM/SIGAPP Symposium on Applied Computing (SAC 2019)

title: Email Business Activities Extraction and Annotation
abstract: Treats organizational emails as resources associated with business activities. It discovers process activities, clusters activity types, and extracts metadata describing those activities, with validation on a public email dataset.

title: Taking Email to Task: The Design and Evaluation of a Task Management Centered Email Tool
abstract: Presents Taskmaster, an email client designed around task management rather than conventional folders and message lists. Its design derives from field research on how workplace email participates in ongoing tasks, and it was evaluated with users managing live email over a two-week period.
venue: Proceedings of the SIGCHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI 2003)

title: Assessing e-mail intent and tasks in e-mail messages
abstract: Studies work tasks and communicative intent in corporate email using Enron and Avocado data. It develops a task taxonomy and manual annotations and examines how work-related email conversations and tasks develop over time, while also evaluating automatic classification across corporate collections.

title: Linking messages and form requests
abstract: Studies an organizational setting in which employees describe tasks by email and instant message to specialists who may need follow-up clarification before completing structured forms. A prototype reads communication and assists with the associated task, providing direct evidence of message-to-business-task association across interactive exchanges.
venue: Proceedings of the 11th International Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces (IUI 2006)

title: Learning information intent via observation
abstract: Studies organizational request messages in which workers ask assistants to perform information-system tasks. The system learns the information intent associated with a request by observing how an expert carries out the corresponding operation, providing direct evidence for mapping workplace messages to concrete tasks.
venue: Proceedings of the 16th International Conference on World Wide Web (WWW 2007)

title: A Hierarchical Distance-dependent Bayesian Model for Event Coreference Resolution
abstract: Introduces a hierarchical distance-dependent Bayesian model for event coreference. Pairwise mention distances are incorporated as learnable Bayesian priors in a nonparametric clustering model, and the approach is evaluated for both within-document and cross-document event coreference on ECB+.
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Cross-document event ordering through temporal, lexical and distributional knowledge
abstract: Studies cross-document event ordering while explicitly addressing event coreference. Event mentions are treated as coreferential when temporal compatibility and semantic compatibility support the same-event interpretation, using lexical and distributional semantic knowledge together with temporal information.

title: Enhancing Cross-Document Event Coreference Resolution by Discourse Structure and Semantic Information
abstract: Improves cross-document event coreference by combining semantic event arguments with document-level discourse structure. Features include agents, patients, times, and locations, while rhetorical structure trees and cross-document lexical chains provide longer-range evidence before mention-pair scoring and clustering.

title: Synergetic Event Understanding: A Collaborative Approach to Cross-Document Event Coreference Resolution with Large Language Models
abstract: Addresses cross-document event coreference as clustering mentions that refer to the same real-world event. The method uses a large language model to generate event-level summaries and transfers that information into smaller-model representations used for coreference decisions.
venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Harvesting Events from Multiple Sources: Towards a Cross-Document Event Extraction Paradigm
abstract: Proposes cross-document event extraction that integrates information about events appearing across multiple documents. Its pipeline includes event extraction, event coreference, entity normalization, role normalization, and entity-role resolution, and it introduces the CLES dataset containing substantial cross-document event structure.
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2024

title: Employing Discourse Coherence Enhancement to Improve Cross-Document Event and Entity Coreference Resolution
abstract: Addresses cross-document coreference where relevant mentions lack a shared coherent document context. The method retrieves additional coherent text, inserts it between mention contexts, and uses the augmented context for event and entity identity decisions, allowing direct evaluation of whether retrieved context improves coreference.
venue: Proceedings of the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: MAVEN-ERE: A Unified Large-scale Dataset for Event Coreference, Temporal, Causal, and Subevent Relation Extraction
abstract: Introduces a unified event-relation dataset with human annotation of event coreference, temporal, causal, and subevent relations. By representing identity and subevent membership as distinct relations within the same event structures, it provides transferable evidence for modeling continuity relations that are not all equivalence relations.
venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

title: Correlating Unlabeled Events at Runtime
abstract: Addresses online assignment of unlabeled process events to process instances. Given a process model, a stream of events without case identifiers, and task-duration information, the approach induces case identifiers with a degree of trust and checks whether resulting executions conform to the model.

title: Event-Case Correlation for Process Mining using Probabilistic Optimization
abstract: Studies recovery of missing case identifiers from timestamped business-process events. It combines a process model, event attributes, constraints, and probabilistic optimization to assign events to cases, and evaluates multiple similarity measures on real-life datasets.

title: Correlating Unlabeled Events from Cyclic Business Processes Execution
abstract: Addresses the problem of reconstructing case identifiers for unlabeled event logs generated by cyclic business processes. The method generates and ranks candidate labeled logs and is evaluated using real-life process data.

title: Surrogate Case Identifier Rules for Construction Site Hoists
abstract: Examines how to construct surrogate process case identifiers when sensor-generated operational events have no native case ID. Multiple candidate case-identification rules are evaluated on a month-long construction-hoist event log, showing that the choice of identity rule can materially alter the resulting process structure.

title: Object-Centric Process Mining: Dealing with Divergence and Convergence in Event Data
authors: Wil M. P. van der Aalst
abstract: Explains why conventional process-mining case notions can distort processes when events relate to multiple business objects. It formalizes convergence and divergence phenomena and advocates event representations in which one event can be associated with objects of several types, providing explicit non-equivalence relation semantics transferable to work-matter modeling.

title: A Framework for Advanced Case Notions in Object-Centric Process Mining
abstract: Studies how sets of related objects in an object-centric event log can be converted into meaningful process executions or cases. It provides a framework for defining, measuring, and optimizing case notions while explicitly considering activity-object relations.

title: An ER-Model-Based Framework for Case Notion Selection in Object-Centric Processes
abstract: Proposes deriving process cases from an entity-relationship schema rather than assuming a single pre-existing case identifier. Cases are constructed from connected components of primary and secondary business entities, making explicit how relational structure induces process-instance identity while avoiding unrestricted resource-based linking.

title: Object-Centric Process Mining: Unraveling the Fabric of Real Processes
authors: Wil M. P. van der Aalst
abstract: Presents object-centric process mining as an alternative to forcing each event into one conventional case. Events may involve any number of business objects of different types, allowing explicit representation of many-to-many event-object relations and the convergence and divergence patterns that result.

title: On-Line New Event Detection and Tracking
abstract: Studies strict online decisions about whether each incoming news story belongs to an already observed event or represents a new event. It combines single-pass clustering with threshold-based new-event detection and evaluates adaptive tracking intended to follow events as they evolve.
venue: Proceedings of the 21st Annual International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval

title: A System for New Event Detection
abstract: Presents an online system that determines whether a story reports an event not previously observed in one or more news streams. It uses incremental TF-IDF representations together with source normalization, inverse-event weighting, and document segmentation and is evaluated on TDT corpora.
venue: Proceedings of the 26th Annual International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval

title: Adaptive online event detection in news streams
abstract: Studies online clustering of news reports that describe the same event. The method adapts event clusters as a stream evolves and includes mechanisms for event merging and noise handling, providing transfer evidence for incremental identity assignment with changing event representations.

title: Topic Detection and Tracking with Time-Aware Document Embeddings
abstract: Develops an online topic-detection and tracking pipeline in which news documents are clustered into events while incorporating temporal proximity into learned representations. The approach is intended to distinguish and track event clusters in streaming data, including recurring events.

title: Tracking the Evolution of Clusters in Social Media Streams
abstract: Studies longitudinal cluster evolution in high-volume social-media streams. The framework explicitly tracks cluster emergence, disappearance, adjustment, splitting, and merging, making it useful as transfer evidence for histories in which a persistent grouping can change structure over time.

title: StableID: An Iterative Graph-Based Framework for Persistent Entity Identification in Evolving Industrial Data Systems
abstract: Addresses persistent entity identifiers in evolving industrial data where newly discovered links can merge previously separate graph components and destabilize identifiers. The framework incorporates historical identity information, applies dominance rules during component merges, and aims to preserve stable and auditable identity over time.

title: Designing Ambiguity-Aware Clerical Review: A Stratified Sampling Framework for Record Linkage and Deduplication
abstract: Studies how limited human-review budgets should be allocated to uncertain candidate record pairs in record linkage. The framework stratifies candidates using match weights, comparison patterns, ambiguity, and demographic groups so that clerical adjudication covers the uncertainty structure rather than simply reviewing the closest-to-threshold pairs.

title: Design-Based Estimation with Record-Linked Administrative Files and a Clerical Review Sample
abstract: Addresses record linkage when automated links contain both erroneous and missing matches. It uses a probability sample subjected to clerical review to establish match status, providing transfer evidence for explicit adjudication of uncertain identity decisions rather than forcing every candidate into match or non-match automatically.

title: Probabilistic record linkage and an automated procedure to minimize the undecided-matched pair problem
abstract: Develops a probabilistic record-linkage procedure for one-to-one matching in the presence of ambiguous candidate pairs. Information from unequivocal matches is used to resolve nonunique or uncertain pairs and reduce the number requiring clerical review, illustrating an explicit undecided region between confident match and non-match.

title: Selective Classification Under Distribution Shifts
abstract: Studies classifiers that can abstain on likely errors when deployment distributions differ from training data. It formulates selective classification under label shift, covariate shift, and out-of-distribution inputs and evaluates confidence-score designs intended to preserve useful risk-coverage behavior under such changes.

title: Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Distribution Shift
abstract: Extends conformal inference to online environments in which the data distribution changes over time. The adaptive procedure continually updates its calibration parameter and provides a long-run coverage guarantee under broad forms of distribution shift, making it relevant to uncertainty management for nonstationary streams.
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems

title: Distance-aware Calibration for Pre-trained Language Models
abstract: Introduces a post-hoc calibration method for pretrained language models that accounts for the distance between test examples and the in-domain training distribution. The method targets overconfidence on shifted and out-of-distribution text and improves calibration and out-of-distribution detection.
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024

title: Phases of Uncertainty: Confidence–Calibration Dynamics in Language Model Training
abstract: Studies how confidence and calibration evolve during language-model training, including behavior under distribution shift. It reports that increasing confidence in later training need not imply improved calibration and motivates calibration strategies that account for changing uncertainty characteristics.
venue: Proceedings of the Workshop on Uncertainty-Aware NLP

title: Supporting Collaborative Task Management in E-mail
abstract: Examines collaborative task management conducted through email, where tasks often require extended interaction rather than a single exchange. The work identifies needs including reminders and the ability to recognize and combine messages related to the same task, and evaluates interfaces intended to support those requirements.

title: Quality Versus Quantity: E-Mail-Centric Task Management and Its Relation With Overload
abstract: Reports field research on professionals using email for task and project management. It identifies multiple challenges arising from complex collaborative work and relates email overload to the qualitative demands of managing tasks and projects rather than message volume alone.

title: Going with the flow: email awareness and task management
abstract: Uses workplace studies to examine how people interleave email with day-to-day ongoing work and maintain awareness of current task focus. It develops a workflow-oriented account of email use and derives design recommendations for supporting task management.
venue: Proceedings of the 2006 20th Anniversary Conference on Computer Supported Cooperative Work (CSCW 2006)
